summary:
Radar for 2026-10-21, GLP-1 focus. The best openings, in order:
(1) The compounded tirzepatide recall. Some headlines (MassLive, Yahoo) say "Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient", which makes people think the branded pens are recalled. They aren't. The recall covers only Apothecary Pharma's compounded vials: Class II, started Sep 24, classified Oct 10. There's also LA Times FOIA reporting on the Chinese ingredient plants. This fits Lane B, but because we already ran a recall Short this week, any long-form has to be the wider "what to check" piece.
(2) Novo's CagriSema analysis in women (REDEFINE 1, about 2,300 women: 25% vs 3% at 68 weeks; by menopause stage 26.7%, 24.8% and 23.1%). It was presented at the Menopause Society on Oct 20, so the 48-hour Lane C window closes Oct 22.
(3) A search-led "semaglutide/tirzepatide and menopause" Lane A long-form. It ties together the Menopause Society news, the Mayo HRT cohort (16% vs 12%, observational) and MedPage/Everyday Health coverage.
(4) Retatrutide gray-market "what's confirmed" ahead of Lilly's Oct 29 earnings. Medscape's plateau piece and MedPage's Reddit side-effects piece keep it rising.
Strong Lane A evergreens that fresh news has revived: GLP-1 supplements (NOW launch and Medical Daily), Ozempic and alcohol (Medscape Oct 21), Ozempic face (Reuters), weight-loss plateaus, the Wegovy pill vs the shot, stopping tirzepatide, and generic semaglutide in Canada.
Rejected: low-dose or "simplified" tirzepatide pieces (they read as a microdosing protocol) and the retatrutide "reconstitution guide" (gray-market how-to).
Not verified: I couldn't get the effect size for the semaglutide handgrip meta-analysis, so scriptwriters need the abstract first. Weekly YouTube counts weren't checked directly; competition ratings come from how heavily the mainstream outlets have covered each topic.

candidates.topic: Is Mounjaro or Zepbound recalled? Only compounded tirzepatide vials from Apothecary Pharma are (Class II, started Sep 24, classified Oct 10, 2026), plus FDA inspection findings at Chinese plants supplying compounding ingredients
candidates.angle: Lane B, 'What's Actually Confirmed?' series: a calm, dated walk-through of what the FDA recall notice says (company, product, 'lack of assurance of sterility', Class II meaning), why headlines saying 'Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient' confused people, what the FDA-cited inspection reports describe (as reported by the LA Times, Oct 19), and how FDA-approved pens differ from compounded vials. Never name a seller. Point viewers to a prescriber about approved options. A recall Short already ran this week, so the long-form must be the wider 'Compounded vs Branded Tirzepatide: What the FDA Has Confirmed' and must add the inspection and import-alert facts.
candidates.why_now: Recall coverage exploded Oct 20–21 (USA Today, Fox Business, NY Post, LA Times, ConsumerAffairs, Times of India). The misleading 'Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient' headlines are sending branded-pen users to search. This is our strongest proven lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed' Shorts: median 108).

evidence.signal: Apothecary Pharma compounded tirzepatide 18 mg/mL vials, 22 lots, Class II, initiated Sep 24, classified Oct 10; not branded Lilly products
Recalls for compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide, plus facility warning letters
FOIA'd FDA inspection reports: mold and insects at Chinese plants making semaglutide/tirzepatide for compounders; both firms on import alert
Headline 'Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised' is the confusion we can correct

candidates.topic: CagriSema in women: Novo's post hoc analysis of REDEFINE 1 (about 2,300 women with obesity or overweight) showed 25% average weight loss vs 3% on placebo at 68 weeks; by menopause stage 26.7% / 24.8% / 23.1% if everyone stayed on treatment (Menopause Society, Oct 20, 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer, new hook first: 'CagriSema for Women: What the New Analysis Shows'. Explain cagrilintide plus semaglutide (amylin plus GLP-1), why this is a post hoc subgroup and not a new trial, the 'if everyone stayed on treatment' estimand vs the overall trial result (22.7% vs 2.3%), the common digestive side effects, and the status: not approved, US decision expected. Don't use the 'Did X beat Y' or 'approved yet?' frames.
keywords: new weight loss drug for women
candidates.why_now: CNBC, BioSpace, Quartz and Invezz covered it Oct 20–21. Health creators haven't covered it yet. The 48-hour first-explainer window closes Oct 22. It overlaps with heavy menopause search interest.

evidence.signal: 25% average weight loss in women at 68 weeks vs 3% placebo, post hoc analysis
Post hoc REDEFINE 1 analysis presented at The Menopause Society Annual Meeting
Most users had digestive side effects (balance line)

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and tirzepatide in menopause: what studies show (Mayo Clinic cohort: semaglutide plus hormone therapy 16% vs 12% without at 12 months, observational; STEP UP/SELECT menopause-stage data; new CagriSema analysis by menopause stage)
candidates.angle: Lane A, search phrase first: 'Ozempic and Menopause: What the Studies Actually Show'. Cover why weight shifts around menopause, what GLP-1 trials show by menopause stage, the hormone-therapy cohort labelled 'linked to' and 'not randomized', and protein and strength training for bone and muscle. End with questions to bring to your doctor, and 'don't start or change hormone therapy on your own'.
candidates.why_now: Menopause Society meeting news (CagriSema), Everyday Health (Oct 20) and MedPage 'GLP-1 in Menopause' (Oct 20) all landed at once. Women 45–65 are a core high-ad-rate audience, and the search demand lasts.

evidence.signal: Combining hormone therapy with GLP-1s may boost weight loss for menopausal women
Wegovy weight loss consistent across menopause stages (STEP UP, SELECT)
Summary of the Mayo semaglutide plus HRT cohort (16% vs 12%), non-randomized

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what the FDA and Lilly have confirmed before Lilly's Oct 29 results (not approved anywhere; filing planned; unverified FDA death reports linked to products sold as retatrutide; Lilly lawsuits; Reddit side-effect reports)
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form 'Retatrutide Online: What the FDA and Lilly Have Confirmed (Oct 2026)'. Every line is attributed and dated. Contrast the trial drug with 'research use only' vials, explain what the Penn AI Reddit study can and can't tell us, and point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or trials. Never name a seller and never explain buying or mixing.
candidates.why_now: MedPage (Oct 20) on retatrutide side effects on Reddit, Medscape (Oct 20) on plateaus, SciTechDaily on the AI Reddit study, NL Times on illegal retatrutide, a flood of search-bait pages, and Lilly's CEO pitching it ahead of Q3 results. Our proven best Short lane.

evidence.signal: Retatrutide side effects on Reddit
Reddit users experimenting with unapproved drug; AI analysis
Illegal retatrutide on the rise in the Netherlands

candidates.topic: Do 'GLP-1 supplements' work like semaglutide? New NOW 'GLP-1 Metabolic Support' launch, a report that about half of GLP-1 users start new supplements (none need FDA approval), and what fibre, protein and eating order really do to your own GLP-1
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'GLP-1 Supplements: Do They Work Like Ozempic?'. Explain natural GLP-1 (minutes) vs semaglutide (a week), what the evidence on fibre and protein preloads shows (modest), how supplement regulation works (DSHEA: no pre-market approval), and the supplements that may matter on treatment (protein adequacy), each with a 'talk to your prescriber' line. Never name a product as an endorsement.
candidates.why_now: A new branded GLP-1 supplement launched Oct 21 (Nutrition Insight) and Medical Daily reported Oct 21 on supplement use among GLP-1 users. It built on Bon Appétit's 'still hungry' test seen in our last snapshot. Big, steady search volume.

evidence.signal: About half of GLP-1 users start new supplements; none need FDA approval
NOW GLP-1 Metabolic Support launch
GLP-1 users increase supplement spend; strong interest in muscle-protecting supplements

candidates.topic: Ozempic and alcohol: what studies show about GLP-1 medicines and drinking (Medscape Oct 21; semaglutide placebo-controlled trial in adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity; Virginia Tech blood-alcohol study; BMJ on a US semaglutide trial on criminal reoffending)
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Ozempic and Alcohol: What the Research Shows'. Separate the RCT (fewer heavy-drinking days) from observational and lab findings, explain the reward-system mechanism simply, note that it's not approved for alcohol use disorder, and give practical safety points (slower absorption, hypoglycemia risk in diabetes, nausea), with a doctor line.
candidates.why_now: Medscape (Oct 21), Medical Economics (Oct 20, semaglutide cuts heavy drinking) and a BMJ news piece (Oct 20) all landed. 'Can you drink on Ozempic' is a perennial high-volume search question, and the holiday season is approaching.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs linked to reduced alcohol consumption
Semaglutide for alcohol use disorder: efficacy and mechanisms
US trial will test whether semaglutide can fight crime

candidates.topic: Weight-loss plateau on tirzepatide or semaglutide: why it happens and what the trials show (Medscape's Oct 20 retatrutide plateau piece as the hook)
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Weight Loss Plateau on Tirzepatide: Why It Happens'. Use the trial weight curves (the flattening around weeks 60–72 in SURMOUNT-1 and STEP 1), metabolic adaptation, and the habits that help (protein, strength training, sleep). Mention retatrutide research only as dated pipeline context. Tell viewers not to change doses or switch on their own, and to talk to their prescriber.
keywords: why did i stop losing weight on zepbound
candidates.why_now: Medscape's Oct 20 piece reframes plateaus around next-gen drugs. 'Mounjaro stopped working' is a huge recurring query from our exact audience, and it fits the long-watch-time explainer lane.

evidence.signal: Could retatrutide break a GLP-1 weight-loss plateau?
Why one-size-fits-all doesn't work for every GLP-1 patient (variable response)

candidates.topic: Ozempic face: what it is, why it happens with fast weight loss, and what the science says (Reuters, Oct 21: beauty companies target the GLP-1 market)
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Ozempic Face: What It Is and What Actually Helps'. Explain that facial volume loss comes from weight loss in general, not from a drug toxin, what's known about speed of loss, and how protein, hydration and strength training help, with a skeptical look at product claims. Strictly no before/after shaming and no product promotion.
candidates.why_now: The Reuters beauty-market story (Oct 21) re-ups one of the highest-volume GLP-1 side-effect searches. A differentiated science angle can win the long-tail clicks.

evidence.signal: Beauty giants target 'Ozempic face' as obesity drug boom opens new market

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide make you weaker? New systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength on semaglutide (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19, 2026), alongside the SEMALEAN cohort (grip strength rose about 4.5 kg at 12 months)
candidates.angle: Muscle outcome question for the Shorts lane ('Semaglutide: Does It Weaken Your Grip?'), then a Lane A long-form, 'Do You Lose Muscle on Semaglutide or Tirzepatide?'. Explain lean mass vs strength, then protein and resistance training (Nutrients rapid review). Scriptwriters must pull the meta-analysis's pooled effect from the abstract before scripting; it wasn't verified here.
keywords: how much weight lost is muscle
candidates.why_now: A fresh meta-analysis (Oct 19) on a proven topic for us (muscle Shorts: 100 and 131 views). Few creators have covered it yet.

evidence.signal: Changes in muscle strength after semaglutide: systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength
Handgrip +4.5 kg at 12 months; sarcopenic obesity 49% to 33% (n=106, uncontrolled)
Protein intake and resistance training across clinical populations

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: what's different (daily vs weekly, the fasting rule, trial results, common side effects), as the pill launches in France without reimbursement and US uptake grows
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Wegovy Pill vs Wegovy Shot: What's the Difference?'. Compare how each is taken, what the trials showed for each in their own populations (indirect comparison, labelled), and side effects. Every piece carries 'don't switch, stop or change on your own; talk to your prescriber'.
keywords: is the wegovy pill as good as the injection
candidates.why_now: Men's Journal (Oct 20) on switching results, a Yahoo Creators doctor explainer (Oct 20) and MedWatch on the France launch (Oct 21). This is the third snapshot in a row showing it, so it's accelerating.

evidence.signal: Wegovy users switched to a daily pill with surprising results
Novo to launch Wegovy pill in France without reimbursement

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide or semaglutide? SURMOUNT-4 and STEP 1 extension regain data, plus AJMC (Oct 20): patients are open to lower-cost maintenance approaches
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'What Happens When You Stop Semaglutide or Tirzepatide?'. Cover the trial regain curves, what partially protected results (habits, strength), and why decisions about maintenance belong with a prescriber. No tapering or dose instructions.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
do you gain weight after stopping wegovy
candidates.why_now: It's been in 6 snapshots with steady momentum. Coverage and price stories (Pennsylvania Medicaid, Belgium reimbursement refusal, UK tirzepatide price rise study) keep pushing people to search about stopping.

evidence.signal: Patients open to lower-cost weight maintenance to expand GLP-1 access
Treatment patterns and weight outcomes before and after a tirzepatide price increase in over 1 million UK self-payers

candidates.topic: Generic semaglutide in Canada: what's changed (IQVIA analysis, Oct 20) and what it means for Canadian patients, alongside Novo's announced US price cuts for 2027 and Pennsylvania Medicaid's 2026 coverage cut
candidates.angle: Lane A, 'What's Actually Confirmed?' style: 'Generic Semaglutide in Canada: What's Confirmed'. Cover Health Canada-approved products only, how generics are reviewed, and that costs and coverage vary. Never name pharmacies or online sources. Mention the US price cuts with dates. Talk to your prescriber or pharmacist.
candidates.why_now: IQVIA's genericization report (Oct 20), the price-cut story seen in 6 snapshots, and Pennsylvania's coverage news (PennLive, Oct 21). Canada is a high-ad-rate core market.

evidence.signal: The genericization of semaglutide in Canada
Pennsylvania Medicaid ended adult GLP-1 coverage for weight loss from Jan 1, 2026; diabetes still covered

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and the heart: ACHIEVE-4 showed non-inferior heart-event risk vs insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (4.2% vs 5.0%), with the CHMP recommendation from Oct 16 and the European Commission decision pending
candidates.angle: Short-form, two-drug body-effect head-to-head naming both sides: 'Orforglipron vs insulin glargine: heart events in type 2 diabetes'. Use the 'non-inferior' wording, flag that the death findings weren't multiplicity-controlled, and list GI side effects. Possible Lane A long-form later: 'Orforglipron (Foundayo): What It Is and Who It's For'.
candidates.why_now: Clinical Trial Vanguard (Oct 19), an OMICS comparison (Oct 20) and the pending EU decision. Orforglipron Shorts have underperformed (35–36), so only use it in the named head-to-head format.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4: MACE 4.2% vs 5.0%, HR 0.84, non-inferior; superiority not shown
Foundayo noninferior to insulin glargine for CV outcomes in diabetes

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and kidneys: new FLOW trial safety analysis by chronic kidney disease severity (Kidney Int, Oct 20), plus real-world tirzepatide kidney outcomes in CKD with type 2 diabetes (Diabet Med, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Single-drug body-effect Short: 'Semaglutide: Is It Safe With Kidney Disease?'. Use the FLOW population (type 2 diabetes plus CKD). Can feed a later Lane A long-form, 'Ozempic and Kidneys: What the FLOW Trial Showed'.
candidates.why_now: Two fresh papers in 48 h on a pillar topic. Kidney searches are evergreen and creator coverage is thin.

evidence.signal: Safety outcomes of semaglutide by CKD severity in FLOW
Real-world kidney outcomes on tirzepatide in CKD with type 2 diabetes and obesity

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and serious mental illness: new JAHA cohort on heart events and death, and a Lancet Psychiatry cohort on psychiatric hospitalisation in schizophrenia with type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: A compassionate, careful explainer: 'Semaglutide and Mental Health: What New Studies Show'. Use observational wording ('linked to'), cover the populations exactly, add 'don't change psychiatric medicines on your own', and include support resources.
candidates.why_now: Two major-journal cohorts in 1 week and the earlier News-Medical explainer. Accelerating slowly (46 to 50 to 48).

evidence.signal: GLP-1 initiation and psychiatric hospitalisation/ED in schizophrenia with type 2 diabetes
GLP-1 RAs and cardiovascular events and death in serious mental illness, type 2 diabetes and obesity

candidates.topic: The GLP-1 gender gap: why men are less likely to be prescribed GLP-1 medicines (Medscape, Oct 21)
candidates.angle: A 'Life on GLP-1' Short: 'Semaglutide and Tirzepatide: Why Fewer Men Take Them'. Cover the prescribing data, how men responded in trials (subgroup averages), and questions to bring to a doctor.
candidates.why_now: Medscape (Oct 21) feature. It pairs naturally with the women/menopause story as a counterpoint.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 gender gap: why are men being left out?

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'Low-dose tirzepatide strategy' content (Endocr Pract real-world cohort in older adults with type 2 diabetes, Oct 15)
candidates.angle: Do not cover. In consumer content it reads as a microdosing or self-titration protocol, which our guardrails ban.
candidates.why_now: Microdosing searches are trending, but the topic breaks the dosing and titration guardrail.

evidence.signal: Low-dose tirzepatide strategy in older adults with type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: REJECT: Retatrutide 'reference vial' reconstitution guide (Apopka Voice, Oct 20)
candidates.angle: Do not cover. It's gray-market how-to and research-chemical SEO bait. Only refer to it as an example inside the Lane B 'what's confirmed' piece, never describing the content.
candidates.why_now: Search-bait pages like this are multiplying with retatrutide interest.
